items.title: CVE-2026-105299 (HIGH 8.7): Summary Before version 0.9.0, the HTTP/1 upstream path in pingora-proxy passed the downstream request through…
items.one_liner: A high-severity header-stripping vulnerability (CVE-2026-105299, CVSS 8.7) in pingora-proxy allows attackers to bypass IP-based authorization in chained proxy deployments.
items.summary: A high-severity vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-105299 (CVSS 8.7) was discovered in pingora-proxy versions prior to 0.9.0. In the HTTP/1 upstream path, Pingora passed downstream requests through upstream_request_filter without removing hop-by-hop headers or connection-nominated headers as mandated by RFC 9110 Section 7.6.1. A remote unauthenticated attacker can exploit this in chained deployments—where an intermediary processes Connection headers and the origin trusts added headers like X-Forwarded-For—to strip security headers and bypass IP-based authorization. Cloudflare CDN customers were unaffected as their internal gateways sanitize connection headers. The issue is resolved in version 0.9.0 by introducing PeerOptions::http_upstream_request_policy to automatically sanitize upstream headers.
key_facts: Affected product: pingora-proxy prior to version 0.9.0
items.bottom_line: Upstream request filtering flaws in proxy implementations can enable remote authorization bypasses if hop-by-hop headers are not properly sanitized.

items.summary: TokenTrap is a new resource-oriented defense mechanism designed to disrupt LLM-based scam systems by forcing them to consume excessive tokens on benign, low-value tasks. items.title: Cisco Secure Client Secure Firewall Posture Module Privilege Escalation Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A local privilege escalation bug in Cisco Secure Client's posture module lets attackers achieve root or SYSTEM privileges.
items.summary: A high-severity privilege escalation vulnerability exists in the interprocess communication channel of the Secure Firewall Posture module in Cisco Secure Client due to insufficient validation of user-supplied input. An authenticated local attacker can exploit this flaw by sending crafted IPC messages to a local socket, allowing them to execute limited file writes with SYSTEM or root privileges. On macOS and Linux, this vulnerability can be leveraged to achieve full root privileges, prompting Cisco to assign it a High Security Impact Rating. Software updates have been released by Cisco to address the issue, as no workarounds are available.

items.title: Amplifying Latency and Cost of LLM Inference via Rowhammer Attack
items.one_liner: DRAM bit-flips in Triton's JIT compilation pipeline can permanently degrade LLM inference performance and corrupt outputs across GPU vendors.
items.summary: Researchers introduce LLVMhammer, the first Rowhammer attack targeting Triton's JIT compilation pipeline to induce bit-flips in CPU DRAM. By altering performance-critical optimization passes in Triton's target-independent stages, the attack forces the framework to generate functionally identical but suboptimal GPU kernels. Because Triton caches generated kernels on disk, a single successful bit-flip causes persistent inference latency degradation ranging from 4% to 16% across subsequent executions on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. Furthermore, the attack can corrupt model outputs, reducing BERTScore to 25%.
items.bottom_line: Rowhammer attacks against Triton compilation caches can persistently slow down LLM inference servers and corrupt model responses.

claims.text: LLVMhammer increases inference latency of an LLM inference server running on a single GPU by 4-16%, which, in turn, can translate into additional annual operating costs at the scale of multi-GPU deployments.

claims.text: We further show that LLVMhammer can also corrupt LLM outputs across different GPU vendors, reducing BERTScore to as low as 25%, illustrating the broader security implications of bit-flips in Triton's compilation pipeline.

items.title: Signal bug could let someone keep listening after you hang up
items.one_liner: Signal vulnerability CVE-2026-113380 allows malicious participants to continue recording audio after a call is terminated.
items.summary: A recently disclosed vulnerability in Signal's calling software, tracked as CVE-2026-113380 with a CVSS score of 9.3, allows a malicious participant to keep listening after a user hangs up. The flaw affects RingRTC versions earlier than 2.72.0 and occurs when an attacker overwhelms a call's internal event queue, interfering with the disconnection process. While message encryption remains secure, the issue can cause audio and potentially video to remain active without the user's knowledge. Developers have updated the underlying library, and users should install the latest app updates to apply the fix.

items.bottom_line: A critical CVSS 9.3 flaw in Signal's call shutdown mechanism can leave audio active after hang-up unless applications are updated.
